issues.description: Field: Animal.name. The problem statement contains two conflicting specifications: the UML diagram (problem_statement.md line 27) shows the attribute as name: String, but the textual Part 1 instruction (problem_statement.md line 85) explicitly asks students to use a StringBuilder for the name attribute. The provided reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 4) declares the field as private String name;. This mismatch (StringBuilder vs String) is actionable and will confuse students about the expected type to implement and how getters/setters should behave.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Choose one of two clear options and apply the changes across artifacts: Option A (use StringBuilder): update the UML in problem_statement.md to name: StringBuilder and change the solution/template Animal.java to declare private StringBuilder name; initialize name = new StringBuilder(inputName) in the constructor; implement getName() to return name.toString(); implement setName(String newName) to assign name = new StringBuilder(newName) or use name.setLength(0); name.append(newName); update any example code/comments accordingly. Option B (use String): remove the textual instruction about StringBuilder from problem_statement.md so the UML and solution remain consistent, and update the task description to request a String. Ensure the template, tests, and example Main.java are aligned with the chosen approach.
